receipt.public_excerpt: there had been a “trend of incidents” in recent months, characterized by a “high blast radius” and “Gen-AI assisted changes” among other factors

evidence_items.explanation: Amazon's own internal briefing note, as reported by the FT, tied a trend of high-impact incidents partly to GenAI-assisted changes.

receipt.public_excerpt: An internal document prepared for the meeting initially identified “GenAI-assisted changes” as a factor in a pattern of incidents stretching back to Q3.

evidence_items.explanation: Indicates that Amazon internally saw AI-assisted changes as a factor in a pattern of incidents over several months.

receipt.public_excerpt: Only one of the incidents involved AI-assisted tooling, which related to an engineer following inaccurate advice that an AI tool inferred from an outdated internal wiki, and none involved AI-written code.

evidence_items.explanation: Amazon says publicly that only one outage involved AI tooling and none involved AI-written code. This undercuts the idea of big AI-caused problems, though it concedes some AI involvement.

receipt.public_excerpt: Amazon acknowledged a limited disruption to a single service in one region last December but attributed it to a user error in configuring access controls, not a flaw in the AI tool itself.

evidence_items.explanation: An earlier AWS incident involved the Kiro AI agent. Amazon calls it limited and blames user error, which bears on how 'big' the AI-linked problems were.

unresolved_gaps: No independent post-mortem says which outage involved AI tooling, or how big that specific outage was.
